title: How to Choose the Right Tire

schwalbeReference.title: Schwalbe tire and inner rim width reference
schwalbeReference.description: This table lists possible combinations of tire widths and inner rim widths for comparison. The listed sizes are possible width pairings, rather than equally suitable choices. See the calculation tab for the best size.
schwalbeReference.hooklessTitle: Tire requirements for hookless / straight side rims
schwalbeReference.hooklessRestriction: Hookless or straight side rims may only be combined with TLE / TLR tires (Tubeless Easy / Tubeless Ready), regardless of whether they are used tubeless or with a tube. This applies to MTB, gravel / cross, city / touring and road bikes.
schwalbeReference.manufacturerNote: Original note: Always consider the maximum air pressure and tire type (Tubeless / Tube Type) specifications of the rim manufacturer.
schwalbeReference.originalPageAlt: Schwalbe's ETRTO 2024 possible tire and inner rim width combinations: 13 tire-width rows, 19 rim-width columns, hookless tire requirements and the 05/2024 publication date
schwalbeReference.datasetName: Schwalbe published ETRTO 2024 possible tire and inner rim width combinations
schwalbeReference.datasetDescription: Thirteen possible-combination rows transcribed from Schwalbe's May 2024 PDF, covering 20–132 mm tire widths and 15–100 mm inner rim widths. This reference retains the original hookless TLE / TLR requirement and manufacturer note.

aero.title: Aero break-through: the 105% flush rule and tire-width calculation
aero.intro: ISO 5775 and ETRTO provide the basis for normal dimensional fitment. The aero target helps select one best width. The 105% relationship applies only up to 30C, and the entered millimetre value is used directly as the tire width.

bulbTire.title: ① The bulb-tire aero failure
bulbTire.formula: Tire wider than the rim's maximum outer width
bulbTire.body: The shoulder rolls outward, flow separates early, and the rim loses much of its aero benefit. Crosswind response can also become less stable.

ruleOf105.title: ② The 105% aero flush rule
ruleOf105.formula: Tire width ≈ maximum rim outer width × 1.05
ruleOf105.body: When the tire is about 5% wider than the rim's maximum outer width, the sidewall transition is closer to flush and flow can stay attached to a more complete teardrop section.

modernSweetSpot.title: ③ The modern hookless road sweet spot
modernSweetSpot.formula: 23–25 mm inner width with a 28–32 mm tire
modernSweetSpot.body: Modern wider rims narrow the engineering window where bead support, rolling resistance, and aero transition work together. A broad chart cannot replace a model-specific limit.

aero.formulaLabel: Tire width and rim outer-width relationship:
aero.currentPairing: Current rim: {rimWidth} mm inner width + about {wallThickness} mm per side = about {rimOuterWidth} mm outer width; 105% aero target tire width = {rimOuterWidth} × 1.05 ≈ {targetTireWidth} mm.

traps.title: Frequent failure modes and workshop lessons

nonTleOnHookless.title: Putting an ordinary clincher with a tube on a hookless rim → sudden unseating
nonTleOnHookless.body: Adding a tube does not give an ordinary clincher the bead tensile strength it lacks. A straight hookless wall still has no mechanical hook to resist pressure and side load.
nonTleOnHookless.rule: Rule: a hookless rim requires a tire with TLE / hookless approval.

emptyTpuInflation.title: Inflating a TPU tube in the air → permanent bulges
emptyTpuInflation.body: An unloaded TPU tube can develop irreversible thin spots and bulges when overinflated. Once installed, the uneven wall can fail on the first ride.
emptyTpuInflation.rule: Rule: stay below 0.3 bar (4.3 PSI) before the tube is inside the tire; never test it with an empty CO₂ blast.

oldSealantResidue.title: Leaving dried sealant in an emergency TPU conversion → abrasion wear
oldSealantResidue.body: Dried latex and grit act like sandpaper against a thin TPU wall as the tire rolls and flexes, often producing a leak within a short ride.
oldSealantResidue.rule: Rule: wipe all dried sealant and grit from the casing before inserting the tube.

co2ColdBrittle.title: Using a CO₂ cartridge aggressively → brittle TPU valve
co2ColdBrittle.body: Rapid CO₂ expansion creates a severe temperature drop. The plastic valve base is more vulnerable to brittle fracture under the cold gas pulse.
co2ColdBrittle.rule: Rule: use a hand pump when possible; use CO₂ with a regulator and a slow release.

metalLever.title: Forcing a tight tire with a metal lever → damaged hookless wall
metalLever.body: A straight hookless lip has no hooked curve to spread a point load. A metal lever can crush or delaminate the carbon edge.
metalLever.rule: Rule: never use a metal lever; push both beads into the center well to release circumference.

beadPinch.title: Pinching the bead seat → tire cannot lock into the safety step
beadPinch.body: A trapped tube prevents the tire from seating evenly. It can wobble under pressure and develop a slow leak.
beadPinch.rule: Rule: stop around 1.0 bar, then inspect the rim line all the way around before final inflation.

examples.title: Fixed combination examples
examples.description: These fixed combinations explain the status labels; the result above updates with your current selection.

critical.title: Hookless · 25 mm inner width × 28 mm tire
critical.description: The ISO table pairs a 25 mm rim with 29–71 mm tires; 28 mm is below that limit.

reference.title: Hookless · 21 mm inner width × 31 mm tire
reference.description: The ISO table pairs a 21 mm rim with 25–65 mm tires. A 31 mm tire is in that normal range, outside the existing 28–30 mm recommendation window.

recommended.title: Hookless · 25 mm inner width × 32 mm tire
recommended.description: A 32 mm tire is inside both the ISO normal range of 29–71 mm and the existing recommendation window of 30–32 mm.

rimSystem.title: Separate TSS from TC first
rimSystem.body: Both inputs use the same nominal-width table here. TSS and TC bead-seat and tire-type requirements must still be checked separately; a width pairing does not grant exact product installation approval.

nominalWidth.title: Selected width is used directly
nominalWidth.body: The selected millimetre value is used directly as tire width; it is not widened again for rim inner width. Confirm actual measurements and product specifications for installation.

aeroProjection.title: 105% explains an aero target only
aeroProjection.body: The relationship here is tire width at about 105% of rim outer width; the derived rim outer width is a display reference for aero shape, not a model-specific result, pressure limit, or bead-retention safety boundary.

items.exactSpecifications: Verify the rim model, tire model, ETRTO, BSD, and the manufacturer's compatibility notes.
items.pressureLimits: Use the strictest limit from the rim, tire, wheelset, and bicycle; this model does not generate a pressure limit.
items.installationCheck: After inflation, check the bead line for even seating, inspect for wobble, and confirm frame and fork clearance.

seo.title: Tire & Rim Width Calculator: ETRTO 2024 Compatibility Chart
seo.description: Find the best tire or rim inner width, check ISO 5775 ranges and simulate hookless fit. Compare DT Swiss and Schwalbe's ETRTO 2024 chart.
seo.articleBody: Normal ranges are looked up in the ISO 5775-1:2023 source width matrix, while the project algorithm selects one best size separately. Users can simulate their selected pairing. DT Swiss TSS and TC tables and Schwalbe's ETRTO 2024 possible-combinations chart, published in May 2024, have separate reference tabs for comparison and source attribution, without a calculation role or exact product certification.
seo.datasetName: Tire and rim engineering reference model with DT Swiss comparison matrix
seo.datasetDescription: Normal widths are looked up in the ISO 5775-1:2023 source matrix. The project algorithm selects a best size separately. DT Swiss tables are static published reference data used for comparison and source attribution.
seo.measurementTechnique: Normal ranges directly use the nominal tire-width and rim-width matrix without interpolation. Best sizes use separate project rules. DT Swiss rows are displayed as published without fitment calculation or interpolation in that reference section.

methodology.title: DT Swiss comparison note
methodology.unavailable: The backend reference matrix is temporarily unavailable. The page keeps the method and safety limits visible and does not substitute example calculation values.
methodology.body: The DT Swiss table shows broad combinations from the published material. Possible rows and interpolated values are comparison references only; they do not decide the engineering model above and are not certification for a specific rim, tire, or wheelset. Follow the exact model limits during installation.
methodology.version: Model version: {modelVersion}. The limitations below come from the same backend contract.

limitations.modelSpecificCertification: This is a DT Swiss reference chart result, not certification for a specific tire, rim model, or wheelset.
limitations.possibleReferenceStatus: Rows marked possible are reference anchors only; they are never relabeled as recommended.
limitations.interpolationProjection: Interpolated widths are mathematical projections between chart rows and must be checked against the exact manufacturer specifications.
limitations.displayOnlyMetrics: The input tire width and the 105%-derived target rim outer-width value are display references, not measured dimensions or safety limits.

standards.title: Manufacturer Standards
standards.description: The following tables show DT Swiss tire and rim inner-width combinations for hookless (TSS) and hooked (TC) systems as a comparison reference. Their ranges are broad guidance and do not replace fitment information for a specific rim and tire model; follow the applicable manufacturers’ limits when installing.
standards.legendDescription: Recommended combinations are DT Swiss preferred pairings. Possible combinations remain chart references; they must not be relabeled as recommendations or treated as model-specific certification.
